absent: Transition preconditions and ordering among context phases and who advances purpose between mount submount and reconfigure.
Semantics and error behavior of each fs_context_operations hook and of get_tree quiet lookup beyond its flag value.
Format severity handling and lifetime rules of fc_log messages and owner module borrowing.
Parsing and matching algorithm for fs_parameter_spec tables and validator success and failure contracts.
Lock ordering and sleep constraints for pin kill, fs_struct sequence access, and fscache volume cookie locks.
Internal fscache acquire relinquish use withdraw lookup resize invalidate and begin operation behavior behind the wrappers.
Meaning and legal combinations of cookie advice bits and volume and cookie flag transitions.
Timestamp copy preconditions and which inode locks if any must be held by stacking callers.

findings.text: Mount configuration context aggregates operation hooks, a userspace mutex, filesystem type link, private areas for filesystem and superblock lookup, root dentry, user and network namespaces, mounter credentials, log prefix plus log pointer, source name, security blob, proposed filesystem info and superblock flags with change mask and extra internal flags, narrow purpose and phase discriminants, and four single bit options for free handling, global namespace use, old API origin, and exclusive creation.

Filesystem customization point is a table of six hooks for releasing a context, duplicating one context into another, parsing one typed parameter, parsing a legacy monolithic blob, materializing the tree, and applying reconfiguration.

Mount parameter record carries a key name, a narrow value kind covering undefined flag string blob filename and file, a variant payload holding one of string pointer blob pointer filename pointer or file pointer, a size extent, and a directory descriptor used with filename values.

Context lifecycle passes through parameter loading for creation, active creation, waiting for mount after creation, waiting for reconfiguration setup, parameter loading for reconfiguration, active reconfiguration, and a terminal failure marker when a transition is invalid.
Context purpose distinguishes three intents: explicit mount needing a new superblock, automatic submount needing a new superblock, and reconfiguration of an existing superblock.

Logging state pairs a constant prefix with a shared log object; the shared log holds a reference count, head and tail insertion and removal indexes, a mask of entries needing release, an owner module for borrowed strings, and eight message slots.

Logging helpers route context or prefix plus format arguments into a common log routine with a severity marker: info uses marker i, warning uses marker w, error uses marker e, and an invalid helper emits an error then yields a negative invalid argument status.
Block device tree lookup quiet behavior is selected by a flag whose numeric value is one.

Directory entry type encoding shifts file mode type bits down by twelve to form the dirent code; mask is the shifted file type mask; codes are unknown zero, fifo one, character two, directory four, block six, regular eight, symlink ten, socket twelve, whiteout fourteen, with maximum sixteen.
Filesystem independent type enumeration runs unknown zero, regular one, directory two, character three, block four, fifo five, socket six, symlink seven, with maximum eight.

Parameter description pairs a name with a validator function pointer, an option number returned on match, flag bits, and opaque data; result of a match records whether a no prefixed negation was used plus one variant outcome among boolean, signed thirty two, unsigned thirty two, unsigned sixty four, user id, or group id.
Parameter description flags use bit one for accepting a no prefixed negation, bit two for permitting an empty value after equals, and bit three for marking a deprecated option.

Typed validators are offered for boolean, unsigned thirty two, signed thirty two, unsigned sixty four, enumeration, string, block device, file descriptor, user id, group id, and file or string alternatives; descriptor construction helpers bind a name and option number to the matching validator with appropriate radix or flag preset for plain flag, negatable flag, octal, hexadecimal, emptyable string, and table driven enumeration.
Description validation helper unconditionally reports success for any supplied name and descriptor table in these fragments.
Pin object used to delay unmount holds a wait queue, a completion flag, two hash list links for superblock and mount membership, and a kill callback invoked to release it.
Pin initializer prepares the wait queue, clears both hash links, and stores the caller supplied kill callback.
Per process filesystem view holds a user count, a sequence lock, a umask, an exec flag, and two path records for root and current directory, with randomized layout.

Init filesystem override swaps the current filesystem view to a shared userspace initial view and returns the prior view; revert checks that the current view is still that shared view and then restores the saved prior view.
Stacking helpers propagate timestamps from a lower inode to an upper inode, either access time alone or access plus modification plus change times together.

Cache instance record holds provider operations, list membership, private provider data, a reference count, atomic counters for active volumes in progress accesses and live objects, a debug identifier, a state discriminant, and a name string.

Cache provider interface names the provider and supplies hooks to acquire and free a volume, look up and withdraw and resize and invalidate a cookie, begin a netfs operation in a requested read write or parameter mode, and prepare a live object for writing.
Cache presence lifecycle moves among not present, preparing, active and usable, stopped after input output error, and withdrawn; count of states is withdrawn plus one.

Cookie lifecycle spans uncached quiescent, lookup, creation, active readable and writable, invalidation, failure requiring withdrawal, least recently used discard, withdrawal, relinquishment, and dropped; state is stored as a single byte and count is dropped plus one.

Volume record holds a reference count, atomic data cookie and in progress access counts, debug and key hash identifiers, key bytes, proc and hash membership, deferred work, owning cache pointer plus cache private pointer, a spin lock, flag word, coherency length, and trailing coherency bytes; flags mark relinquished, invalidated, collided, acquire pending, and creating.

Cookie record holds reference and activity and access counts, debug and invalidation identifiers, a spin lock, parent volume link, cache private pointer, hash proc and commit membership, deferred work, object size, last unused time, flag word, single byte state, advice byte, key and auxiliary lengths and hash, and two variants each either holding an external pointer or short inline bytes for key and auxiliary data; flags track relinquished retired caching empty update cached disabled local write no wake and pending relinquish withdraw discard prepare write invalidate plus data present and hashed markers.

Cache advice uses bit zero for single chunk objects, value zero to cache on local write, bit one to avoid caching on local write, and bit two to request runtime cache size retrieval; direct write invalidation marker has value one; desired operation modes are parameters, write, and read.

Two build configurations exist: enabled reports availability as true and treats non null volume cookie and cache private resource as valid with enabled meaning present and disabled bit clear; disabled reports availability as false and treats every volume cookie resource and enabled test as false or zero.

Volume and cookie acquisition wrappers return null without further work when the subsystem is unavailable or the parent handle is invalid, otherwise they forward keys coherency advice sizes and auxiliary data to internal acquisition; relinquish and use wrappers only forward when the supplied handle tests valid.

Key accessor returns inline storage for short keys and the external pointer otherwise; resource to cookie accessor follows the cache private field; object accounting increments on count, decrements with a wake of clearance waiters on reaching zero, and a waiter blocks until the live object count reaches zero.

Cookie state reader performs an acquire ordered load of the state field; statistics helpers either bump global read write no space culled and misfit counters or compile to no operation depending on configuration.

Userspace access to a mount context is serialized by its dedicated mutex; per process root and current directory reads are guarded by a sequence lock; cache volume and cookie mutation is guarded by per object spin locks while lifetime uses reference counts and atomic access and object counters with waiter wakeup at zero.

Inline versus external key and auxiliary selection depends on length thresholds of sixteen and eight bytes, so callers must not retain the returned key pointer across cookie mutation; shared log holds only eight slots with head tail wraparound and selective freeing, so overflow and ownership handling need care.
